description: In 1923, the Orient Express arrives in Trieste, an unusually strong Bora envelops the entire city. Hotel staff confirm the wind is "strangely sinister." The investigators step into this port city, getting their first sense of the supernatural.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: A new story begins, wish you all a pleasant journey! Recording of "Cold Wind Howls - Trieste 1923" has now started... Wait, a piece of paper flew out... Boring! I want to see bloodshed!

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The Orient Express arrived in Trieste at 7:54 PM sharp. The investigators stepped through the train doors under the station's dome, first feeling the wind. It roared like an angry beast across the platform, piercing through clothing and sucking away the warmth from their bodies. Loose dirt and branches whistled through the air, occasional strong gusts shaking loose parts of the roof, making the entire structure vibrate and echo. Porters in tightly buttoned overcoats helped with luggage, finally guiding everyone to the waiting room for shelter. Both porters and passengers cursed this wind, calling it the Bora, a common phenomenon in the region. At night, only motorized vehicles were visible; all horse-drawn carriages had gone home.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "This magical weather really isn't very suitable for human survival. This wind is indeed a bit strong." #Check if there are any drivers nearby still taking passengers.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Nods silently, tightening the trench coat.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Fortunately, there's no land desertification or sand around here. Otherwise, in this situation, a sandstorm would be quite deadly."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "The professor is still knowledgeable and well-informed."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Three drivers in leather jackets huddled in a sheltered corner smoking, the embers of their cigarettes glowing and fading in the gloom. A fat man wrapped in a scarf was waving his arms, telling some story, while the two beside him coughed and nodded. Behind them, the sheet metal roofs of three Fiat 509s flapped loudly in the wind, with one's hood still emitting white steam.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Approach this fat man.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Also, you recall the professor's notes: visiting someone named Winkelmann might be helpful. But it's already late today. Finding a hotel to stay and setting out tomorrow is a good plan.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Poke Gang. "What's he saying? Can we rent a car?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Hmm, we might need some means of transport to take us to a hotel."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Listen.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The fat man noticed player4 and stood up, then crushed his cigarette butt under his shoe. Three silver lire for three kilometers! This damn weather, cash only—where are you gentlemen headed? His yellowish fingernails gripped the car door handle.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Convert the price.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Silver lire?" #player4 can remember fiercely double-crossing a greedy tour guide in Venice and robbing him of all his money. #Thus, takes out 9 lire in banknotes from the ill-gotten gains.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Presses down on his hat. "Brother, business isn't easy, huh?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The driver's greasy fingers snatched the nine-lire note, which rustled in the wind. He stuffed it into his leather jacket pocket, a dry, raspy laugh grating from his throat. Yeah... but I have a wife and kids to feed. Get in! He pulled open the Fiat's door, its hinges groaning with rust.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Big brother, find us a hotel."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Hey, driver, do you know of any hotels nearby you'd recommend?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The driver turned the key. The Fiat's engine coughed and rattled, then rumbled to life, the car body swaying slightly in the wind. The exhaust pipe belched choking black smoke. He glanced through the rearview mirror. The Central Hotel, of course. Right by the main square, clean and cheap. At night, you can hear the waves from the harbor. He stepped on the gas, tires crunching over gravel on the platform, the Bora wind thumping dully against the car windows.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Alright, let's go there then."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The Fiat bumped along the harbor, its headlights cutting swathes of dim yellow light on the wet cobblestones. Ten minutes later, the car braked to a stop in front of a four-story stone building. A brass plaque on the arched portico read "Central Hotel." A bellboy in gold-trimmed uniform hurried down the rain-washed steps, the Bora whipping the ribbons on his cap. His black leather shoes splashed into a puddle, sending up silvery spray. "Here we are, the Central Hotel." In the distance, golden warm light from a crystal chandelier shone through the brass revolving door.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: #Go to the trunk to get the luggage. #Say to Xiao Tang.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: #Get the luggage and prepare to get off the car to book a room.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Show some awareness. Shouldn't you perform well in front of the professor?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "It's fine, minor issue. The stuff isn't heavy anyway." "Let's go in first."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The bellboy deftly takes the luggage. The revolving door shuts out the Bora's howl. The glow from the crystal chandelier spills over the marble pillars. The brass bell on the front desk tinkles lightly. Behind the oiled walnut counter stands a gray-haired manager. Welcome to the Central Hotel, his Adam's apple bobs as his gaze sweeps over the five's dust-covered coats. Would you like adjoining rooms?

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Also place the still drowsy Johnson onto Xiao Tang

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "If we can be adjacent, that would be even better."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Alright. The manager's pen nib rustles across the ledger. Three brass keys are handed to you, their serrated teeth holding enamel number plates for 203-205. Top floor, facing south, sheltered from the wind. The manager pushes his tortoiseshell glasses up with his index finger. Luggage will be delivered to the rooms—suggest everyone lock the windows tight, tonight's Bora could blow the chimneys into the Adriatic Sea.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Thank you, may God bless you."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #Feels for the cigarettes, decides it's really not a good idea, and puts them back.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Let's go, choose rooms first."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "By the way, has the wind been this strong all this time?"

The masts of ocean-going freighters pierce the sky like fingers, anchor chains clang in the gale. At the end of the breakwater, the lighthouse beam flickers intermittently through the spray. Three steam barges rock and sway by the dock.

conversation.text: player4 sinks into the down pillow, dark circles under his eyes. Morning light pierces through the gaps in the brocade curtains onto his face. His fingers rub his temples with a neurotic tremor. After getting up, the mirror reflects his slipping collar. He tries to recall the dream, only grasping fragments: a darkness, swirling waters, the screams of creatures.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: #Cold sweat almost instantly soaks through the thin pajamas, sticking clammily to the skin, then chilled by the endless cold emanating from within. Curled up in the corner of the bed, teeth chattering uncontrollably, every breath carries a tearing pain, as if inhaling not air but countless tiny ice shards, cutting into fragile lungs. Consciousness floats and sinks in the tide of agony, black shadows begin to creep at the edges of vision. Subconsciously grabs the diary by the bedside. Moonlight seeps coldly through the window crack, illuminating the girl's face, pale as paper.
